Ammolite.description: organic gemstone formed when it mixes with fossilized shell of extinct marine ammonite

Beach Glass.description: pieces of glass that have been naturally weathered by water

Borax.description: mineral (as opposed to the chemical compound)

Breccia.description: rock composed of angular fragments in a groundmass

Carnelian.description: yellow-red chalcedony variety, used as a semi-precious gemstone

Clear Quartz.description: colourless and transparent form of quartz

Coal Ball.description: stone of peat that did not turn into coal

Coquina.description: sedimentary rock that is composed mostly of fragments of shells

Desert Rose.description: rose-like formations of crystal clusters of gypsum or baryte which include abundant sand grains

Diorite.description: deep igneous rocks made of equal amounts of alkali feldspar and intermediate plagioclase, the most common stained ingredients are amphibole, biotite and pyroxene, and accessory minerals apatite and sfen; volcanic equivalent: tackle.

Fulgurite.description: metamorphic rock formed when lightning strikes sand, soil, sand, rock, organic debris

Goethite.description: iron(III) oxide-hydroxide named in honor to the poet Goethe

Goldstone.description: glittering glass made in a low-oxygen reducing atmosphere

titles.jawiki: ゴールドストーン (宝石)

Granite.description: common type of intrusive, felsic, igneous rock with grained texture

Gypsum Rose.description: rose-like formations of crystal clusters of gypsum or baryte which include abundant sand grains

Iolite.description: gem variety of the mineral cordierite

Iron Meteorite.description: meteorite composed of iron-nickel alloy called meteoric iron

Lapis Lazuli.description: contact metamorphic rock containing lazurite (but in most cases is haüyne), pyrite and calcite, mainly

Larimar.description: blue gemstone from the Dominican Republic

Larvikite.description: igneous rock, variety of syenite or monzonite

Limestone.description: sedimentary rocks made of the chemical substance calcium carbonate

Marble.description: foliated metamorphic rock of carbonatic minerals

Onyx Marble.description: banded carbonate rock that forms mainly around hot springs; typically used as a decorative or architectural material or for small ornamental objects

Opalite.description: Trade name for opal and moonstone simulants

Precious Opal.description: Precious opal shows a variable interplay of internal colors, and though it is a mineraloid, it has an internal structure.

Pumice.description: light coloured highly vesicular volcanic rock

Red Ochre.description: iron oxide red pigment made from clay or by calcining selected grades of yellow ocher

Siltstone.description: sedimentary rock which has a grain size in the silt range (per ISO 14688 between 0.002 and 0.063 mm)

Slate.description: fine-grained, foliated, homogeneous, low-grade metamorphic rock

Stony Meteorite.description: meteorite predominantly made of silicate minerals

Stromatolite.description: layered sedimentary rock structure of biological origin

Sunstone.description: brown-orange plagioclase (oligoclase, mainly) feldspar variety with hematite

Tanzanite.description: blue to purple variety of the mineral zoisite

Tektite.description: glassy body formed by a meteorite impact

Thulite.description: manganese-bearing, pink- to red-colored variety of the mineral zoisite

Travertine.description: form of terrestrial limestone deposited around mineral springs, especially hot springs
